summary:
Astpreneurs is an interactive educational platform designed to bring the fascinating stories of NASA's space exploration hardware to life for younger generations to make them aware of NASA's old space explorations. 

Our project addresses the challenge of making NASA's abandoned, retired, and still-operational space equipment more accessible, engaging, and memorable. Through an interactive website, users discover eight remarkable spacecraft and scientific instruments associated with the Moon, Mars, and deep space.

Each spacecraft features a four-part illustrated story explaining its origins, technology, scientific discoveries, and current status. To make learning more enjoyable, we developed eight unique mission-inspired mini-games. By completing these challenges, users collect puzzle pieces to assemble their own Space Explorer Badge.

Using information from NASA's official mission resources, Astpreneurs combines scientific storytelling, interactive gameplay, and visual learning to inspire curiosity about space exploration and preserve the legacy of historic space missions.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

Astpreneurs is an interactive educational website created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, addressing the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars."

Our goal is to bring the stories of space exploration hardware to life and help younger generations understand the scientific discoveries, engineering achievements, and lasting legacy of NASA missions.

Users begin by exploring a colorful, interactive gallery organized into three destinations: the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space.

The platform features eight interactive mission experiences: the Apollo 11 Lunar Laser Retroreflector, Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Opportunity, InSight, Curiosity, Ingenuity, Voyager 1 2, and Cassini.

Each mission includes a four-part illustrated story that introduces the spacecraft or instrument, explains how its technology works, highlights its scientific discoveries, and describes its mission status or legacy.

After reading a story, visitors can play a unique mission-inspired mini-game. For example, users can aim laser beams toward the Apollo 11 lunar reflector, experience challenges inspired by Mars exploration, and complete activities related to other missions.

Each successfully completed mini-game unlocks a piece of an eight-part Space Explorer Badge. Collecting all eight pieces gives learners an additional goal and encourages them to explore every mission.

What benefits does it have?

Many people recognize famous NASA missions but know little about the instruments and spacecraft that made their discoveries possible. Some equipment remains on the lunar or Martian surface long after its mission has ended, while other spacecraft continue operating or have left a lasting scientific legacy.

Thanks to Antprenuers young generations learn and acknowledge the some interesting NASA missions and their willingness to learn about these subjects increase. Instead of presenting only facts and dates, we combine visual storytelling, interactive challenges, and rewards to encourage curiosity about space science, engineering, and exploration history.

The project is designed especially for students, young space enthusiasts, and anyone interested in discovering how space technology works.

What is the intended impact of the project?

Our main goal is to make learning about space more fun and interesting, especially for students and young people like us. We want to show that the equipment NASA left on the Moon and Mars is not just space junk, but an important part of space exploration history.

As students from Türkiye, we are inspired by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk's words, "İstikbal göklerdedir" ("The future is in the skies"). This quote reminds us how important science, technology, and space exploration are for the future.

Through our stories and mini-games, we hope to inspire more young people to become curious about space and maybe even dream of becoming scientists or engineers one day. Even if our project makes one student more interested in space, we would consider that a success.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

We had some experience with Python, but we didn't know much about web development. That's why we used Google Gemini to help us build our project. Gemini helped us write and understand the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript code for our website and mini-games.

We used AI to turn our ideas into a working project. We also used GitHub Pages to publish our website so everyone can access it for free. During this project, we learned more about web development and how AI can help with coding.

How is your project creative?

We think our project is creative because we turned NASA's space equipment into interactive stories and games. Instead of just reading information, users can explore different missions and learn while playing.

We also created a badge system where players collect a puzzle piece after completing each mini-game. This makes learning more fun and encourages users to explore all eight missions.

We wanted to make something that feels like a space adventure rather than a regular educational website.

What factors did your team consider?

While developing our project, we wanted to make sure that it was fun, educational, and easy to use. We thought about how to make space exploration interesting for students, especially those who don't know much about NASA missions.

We tried to keep the stories simple and understandable while using NASA's official resources to make the information reliable. We also wanted the website to be colorful and interactive so users wouldn't get bored.

Since we were still learning web development, we tried to make a project that we could build and improve with the help of AI.
